learning_outcomes.text: To know, understand and apply the basic concepts of fluid mechanics for professional development in engineering in the field of fluids.
To apply the strategies of scientific methodology in fluid mechanics: to qualitatively and quantitatively analyze the problem situation, to formulate hypotheses and solutions.
To adequately communicate knowledge, procedures, results, skills and aspects inherent to fluid mechanics, using specific vocabulary and terminology and appropriate means.
To work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the development of fluid mechanics work, adopting a responsible, orderly attitude and willingness to learn.

To plan and develop designs and processes in the field of fluid mechanics according to the corresponding specific technology, applying quality principles and methods and analyzing and assessing the social and environmental impact of the technical solutions applied.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fluid mechanics. Previous concepts. Introduction to the fundamental previous concepts for the study of Fluid Mechanics.
Physical properties of fluids. Definitions. Analysis of the fundamental physical properties of fluids.
General laws of fluid statics. Obtaining the fundamental equation of fluid statics from the classification of forces acting on fluids.

Statics of an incompressible fluid in the gravitational field. Hydrostatics. Obtaining the fundamental equation of hydrostatics. Analysis of its consequences and its application to pressure measurement.
Fluid statics in other force fields. Relative equilibrium. Study of liquids subjected to uniform rotation and uniform translation.
Statics of compressible fluids in the gravitational field. Analysis of pressure variation in compressible fluids.
Forces on surfaces. Calculation of the force and the point of application of fluids on flat and curved surfaces.
Forces on closed bodies. Calculation of forces exerted by fluids on closed bodies.
Fundamentals of fluid motion. Introduction to the fundamental concepts for the study of fluid motion.
Mass conservation theorem. Continuity equation. Obtaining the mass conservation theorem and the continuity equation.
Fundamental equations of fluid dynamics. Presentation of Euler's equations of motion along a trajectory and Navier-Stokes equations.
Bernoulli's Equation. Obtaining the different forms of the energy equation or Bernoulli's equation and introduction to the concepts of power and efficiency in pumps and turbines.
Applications of Bernoulli's equation. Measuring devices. Application of Bernoulli's equation for determining the velocity and flow rate of a fluid.
Momentum and angular momentum theorems. Obtaining the momentum and angular momentum theorems.
Applications of the momentum theorem. Presentation of several technical applications of the momentum theorem.
Dimensional analysis and dynamic similarity. Introduction to the concepts of dimensional analysis and dynamic similarity, Buckingham's theorem and its application to the design of hydraulic machines.
Effects of viscosity on flows. Study of external flows, focusing on the concepts of boundary layer, drag, and lift.
Study of head losses in closed conduits. Introduction to the fundamental equations and diagrams for calculating head losses in closed conduits.
Steady flow of fluids in closed conduits. Practical calculation of pipelines. Networks. Calculation of series, parallel, branched, and meshed pipe systems.
Transient flow in pipes. Calculation of water hammer and its protection.
Steady flow in open conduits. Channels. Calculation of head losses in open conduits.

Hydraulic machinery. Fundamental principles. Turbomachinery. Introduction to the fundamental concepts related to hydraulic machines, focusing on turbomachinery, as well as the phenomenon of cavitation.

Hydraulic turbines. Hydroelectric power plants. Analysis of the fundamental types of hydraulic turbines, their fields of application, their constitutive elements, and their application to hydroelectric power plants.
Hydraulic pumps. Description of the fundamental types of hydraulic pumps, their operating principle, and the field of use for each.
Pumping installations. Constitutive elements, characteristic curves, and selection of pumps for a pumping installation.
assessment_rules: The continuous assessment system includes a written theory and problem exam (70%), an individual exam on practicals (20%), and assignments and continuous assessment tests (10%). To pass, students must score at least 4 out of 10 points on the written exam. For the extraordinary examination, positive results obtained during the course from continuous assessment (up to 30% for lab practices and other continuous assessment tests) may be carried over. If negative results were obtained through continuous assessment, they will not be retained, and the student may obtain 100% of the grade through a new comprehensive assessment.
